Re-run here on the store file with ffmpeg 8.1.2: `ffmpeg -i tos-action-30s.mp4 -an -vf "scdet=threshold=8,metadata=print:file=-" -f null -` reports cuts at 10.291667 s and 18.916667 s (frames 247 and 454 at 24 fps), matching OT-3.

method: All times (t_s) are SOURCE-clip seconds of tos-action-30s.mp4, not timeline seconds; each sample is the exact frame n = 24 x t_s. Samples run on the 0.5 s grid inside the shot (10.5-18.5 s, 17 samples). Each frame was viewed at source resolution with a 100 px reference grid (early frames also as 2x crops with a 50 px grid), and the point is the centre of the bounding box of the visible robot body, limbs and mounted weapon included, in source pixels (origin top-left). Lower legs partly hidden in rubble are judged by the visible part. Precision is about +-25 px. Samples where the robot is not identifiable have x and y null with a note; a test should count only non-null samples, or state how it treats the nulls. Checked by drawing the points on 4 frames and viewing them.
